rule_en: 1st house: life, stature, colour, complexion, form and shape of the querent/native (in mundane charts the common people). Rules head and face; colour white; masculine; consignificators Aries and Saturn; Mercury has his joy here; called the Ascendant.
quote: It hath signification of the life of man, of the stature, colour, complexion, forme and shape of him that propounds the Question, or is borne
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.50 [PDF p.84]; consignificators/joy/colour on p.51
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 2nd house: estate, wealth or poverty, moveable goods, money lent, profit or loss; in lawsuits the querent's friends/assistants; in duels the querent's second. Neck; green; feminine, succedent ('Anaphora'); consignificators Jupiter and Taurus; Sun and Mars never well placed here (dispersion of substance).
quote: From this house is required judgment concerning the estate or fortune of him that asks the Question, of his Wealth or Poverty, of all moveable Goods, Money lent, of Profit or gaine, losse or damage
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.51 [PDF p.85]; continues p.52
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 3rd house: brethren, sisters, kindred, neighbours, short/inland journeys, frequent removing, letters, rumours, messengers. Shoulders, arms, hands, fingers; red and yellow; cadent; masculine; consignificators Gemini and Mars; joy of the Moon.
quote: Hath signification of Brethren, Sisters, Cozens or Kindred, Neighbours, small Journeys, or inland-Journeys, oft removing from one place to another, Epistles, Letters, Rumours, Messengers
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.52 [PDF p.86]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 4th house: fathers, lands, houses, tenements, inheritances, tillage, hidden treasure, the end of any matter; towns and castles besieged. Breast, lungs; red; feminine; North angle (Imum Coeli); consignificators Cancer and the Sun; father signified also by Sun by day, Saturn by night.
quote: Giveth Judgment of Fathers in general, and ever of his Father that enquires, or that is borne; of Lands, Houses, Tenements, Inheritances, Tillage of the earth, Treasures hidden, the determination or end of any thing
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.52 [PDF p.86]; continues p.53 (Sun by day, Saturn by night signify fathers)
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 5th house: children, ambassadors, a woman with child, banquets, ale-houses, taverns, plays, messengers; the father's wealth. Stomach, liver, heart, sides, back; masculine; succedent; consignificators Leo and Venus (Venus joys here); Mars or Saturn here show disobedient children.
quote: By this house we judge of Children, of Embassadours, of the state of a Woman with child, of Banquets, of Ale-houses, Tavernes, Playes
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.53 [PDF p.87]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 6th house: servants, small cattle, sickness (its quality, cause, curability, length), tenants, farmers, uncles (father's siblings). Lower belly and intestines; feminine, cadent, unfortunate (no aspect to the Ascendant); black; Mars rejoices here; consignificators Virgo and Mercury.
quote: It concerneth Men and Maid-servants, Galliflaves, Hogges, Sheep, Goats, Hares, Connies, all manner of lesser Cattle, and profit or losse got thereby; Sicknesse, its quality and cause
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.53 [PDF p.87]; continues p.54
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 7th house: marriage and the person inquired after, love questions, open enemies, the defendant, the opposing party in war, quarrels, lawsuits, the astrologer himself, thieves, wives and sweethearts, fugitives. Haunches to buttocks; dark black; masculine; West angle; consignificators Libra and the Moon; Saturn or Mars unfortunate here show ill in marriage.
quote: It giveth judgement of Marriage, and describes the person inquired after, whether it be Man or Woman, all manner of Love questions, our publique enemies
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.54 [PDF p.88]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: The consignificator glyph after Libra is a crescent (Moon) in the image.

rule_en: 8th house: estate of the dead, death and its quality, wills and legacies, dowry of the wife, the adversary's second, defendant's friends, fear and anguish of mind, heirs. Privy parts; green and black; consignificators Scorpio and Saturn; succedent, feminine.
quote: The Estate of Men deceased, Death, its quality and nature; the Wils, Legacies and Testaments of Men deceased; Dowry of the Wife, Portion of the Maid
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.54 [PDF p.88]; ends p.55
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 9th house: long voyages, religion and clergy, dreams, visions, foreign countries, books, learning, church livings, the wife's kindred. Fundament, hips, thighs; green and white; consignificators Sagittarius and Jupiter; the Sun rejoices here; masculine, cadent.
quote: By this House we give judgement of Voyages or long journies beyond Seas of Religious men, or Clergy of any kinde, whether Bishops or inferiour Ministers; Dreames, Visions, forraigne Countries, of Books, Learning
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.55 [PDF p.89]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 10th house: kings, princes, magistrates and officers in authority, mothers, honour, preferment, dignity, office, lawyers, the profession or trade. Knees and hams; red and white; feminine; Medium Coeli; consignificators Capricorn and Mars; Jupiter or the Sun here fortunate, Saturn or the Dragon's Tail usually deny honour.
quote: all sorts of Magistracy and Officers in Authority, Mothers, Honour, Preferment, Dignity, Office, Lawyers; the profession or Trade any one useth
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.55 [PDF p.89]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 11th house: friends and friendship, hope, trust, confidence, praise or dispraise, fidelity of friends; a king's favourites, counsellors, treasure. Legs to the ankles; saffron/yellow; consignificators Aquarius and the Sun; Jupiter especially rejoices here; succedent, masculine, 'in vertue' equivalent to the 7th or 4th.
quote: It doth naturally represent Friends and Friendship, Hope, Trust, Confidence, the Praise, or Dispraise of any one; the Fidelity or falsenesse of Friends
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.56 [PDF p.90]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: 12th house: private enemies, witches, great cattle, sorrow, tribulation, imprisonment, all affliction, self-undoing, secret informers. Feet; green; consignificators Pisces and Venus; Saturn much joys here; cadent, feminine ('Cataphora').
quote: It hath signification of private Enemies, of Witches, great Cattle, as Horses, Oxen, Elephants, &c. Sorrow, Tribulation, Imprisonments, all manner of affliction, self-undoing
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.56 [PDF p.90]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Lilly presents these house meanings as Ptolemaic doctrine confirmed by his own practice and explicitly sets aside the Arabian subdivisions of the houses.
quote: This is the true Caracter of the severall Houses, according to the Ptolomeian Doctrine, and the experience my selfe have had for some yeers
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VII 'Of the twelve Houses, their Nature and signification', p.56 [PDF p.90]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Houses Capricorn (night) and Aquarius (day); exalted in Libra; fall in Aries; rejoices in Aquarius; rules the airy triplicity by day. Course 29 years 157 days; middle (mean) motion 2'01" per day; daily motion 3-6'.
quote: Capricorne ♑ his Night-house, Aquarius ♒ his Day-house; he is Exaltated in ♎, he receives his Fall in ♈
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VIII 'Of the Planet Saturne, and his signification', p.57 [PDF p.91]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: Detriment is not stated in this chapter (see p.104 table, other session).

rule_en: Diurnal, cold and dry, melancholic, earthly, masculine; the greater infortune; author of solitariness.
quote: He is a Diurnall Planet, Cold and Dry (being farre removed from the heat of the Sun) and moyst Vapours, Melancholick, Earthly, Masculine, the greater Infortune, author of Solitarinesse, Malevolent
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VIII 'Of the Planet Saturne, and his signification', p.58 [PDF p.92]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Well dignified: profound imagination, severe in acts, reserved in words, patient in labour, grave in dispute, studious of worldly goods, austere.
quote: Then he is profound in Imagination, in his Acts severe, in words reserved, in speaking and giving very spare, in labour patient, in arguing or disputing grave
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VIII 'Of the Planet Saturne, and his signification', p.58 [PDF p.92]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Ill dignified: envious, covetous, jealous, mistrustful, timorous, sordid, dissembling, sluggish, suspicious, stubborn, malicious, never contented.
quote: Then he is envious, covetous, jealous and mistrustfull, timorous, sordid, outwardly dissembling, sluggish, suspitious, stubborne, a contemner of women, a close lyar, malicious, murmuring, never contented, ever repining
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. VIII 'Of the Planet Saturne, and his signification', p.58 [PDF p.92]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Houses Sagittarius (day) and Pisces (night); course 12 years; middle motion 4'59".
quote: He hath two of the twelve Signs of the Zodiack for his houses, viz. ♐ his Day-house, and ♓ his Night-house
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. IX 'Of the Planet Jupiter, and his signification', p.61 [PDF p.95]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Detriment Gemini and Virgo; exalted in Cancer; fall in Capricorn; rules the fiery triplicity by night.
quote: He receives Detriment in ♊ and ♍: He is Exalted in ♋, hath his Fall in ♑
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. IX 'Of the Planet Jupiter, and his signification', p.62 [PDF p.96]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Diurnal, masculine, temperately hot and moist, airy, sanguine; the greater fortune; author of temperance, modesty, sobriety, justice.
quote: He is a Diurnall, Masculine Planet, Temperately Hot and Moyst, Aiery, Sanguine, the greater Fortune, author of Temperance, Modesty, Sobriety, Justice
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. IX 'Of the Planet Jupiter, and his signification', p.62 [PDF p.96]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Well placed: magnanimous, faithful, bashful, honourably aspiring, a lover of fair dealing, wishing to benefit all, religious, affable, charitable, just, wise, prudent.
quote: Then is he Magnanimous, Faithfull, Bashfull, Aspiring in an honourable way at high matters, in all his actions a Lover of faire Dealing, desiring to benefit all men
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. IX 'Of the Planet Jupiter, and his signification', p.62 [PDF p.96]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Unfortunate: wastes his patrimony, lets everyone cozen him, hypocritically religious, obstinate in false tenets, ignorant, careless, dull, schismatical, abasing himself.
quote: When ♃ is unfortunate, then he wastes his Patrimony, suffers every one to cozen him, is Hypocritically Religious, Tenacious, and stiffe in maintaining false Tenents in Religion
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. IX 'Of the Planet Jupiter, and his signification', p.63 [PDF p.97]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Houses Aries (day) and Scorpio (night); exalted 28 Capricorn; 'depressed' (fall) 28 Cancer; detriment Libra and Taurus; rules the whole watery triplicity (day and night). Course 1 year 321 days; mean motion printed '31 degr. 27 min.' (i.e. 31'27" per day); retrograde 80 days.
quote: He hath ♈ for his Day-house, and ♏ for his Night-house; he is exalted in 28 degr. of ♑, and is depressed in 28 ♋, he receiveth detriment in ♎ and ♉
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. X 'Of the Planet Mars, and his severall significations', p.65 [PDF p.99]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: Mean motion is printed as '31 degr. 27 min.'; context (daily motion 32-44 min.) shows minutes are meant.

rule_en: Masculine, nocturnal, hot and dry, choleric and fiery; the lesser infortune; author of quarrels, strifes, contentions.
quote: He is a Masculine, Nocturnall Planet, in nature hot and dry, cholerick and fiery, the lesser Infortune, author of Quarrels, Strifes, Contentions
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. X 'Of the Planet Mars, and his severall significations', p.66 [PDF p.100]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Well dignified: invincible in war and courage, bold, confident, immovable, contentious, valiant, obeys no one, boasts of his acts, yet prudent in his own affairs.
quote: In feats of Warre and Courage invincible, scorning any should exceed him, subject to no Reason, Bold, Confident, Immoveable, Contentious, challenging all Honour to themselves
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. X 'Of the Planet Mars, and his severall significations', p.66 [PDF p.100]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Ill placed: prattler without modesty or honesty, lover of slaughter and quarrels, murder, thievery, sedition; highway thief, traitor, perjured, rash, inhumane, treacherous, violent.
quote: Then he is a Pratler without modesty or honesty, a lover of Slaughter and Quarrels, Murder, Theevery, a promoter of Sedition, Frayes and Commotions, an Highway-Theefe
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. X 'Of the Planet Mars, and his severall significations', p.66 [PDF p.100]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Only house Leo, detriment Aquarius; exalted 19 Aries, fall 19 Libra; rules the fiery triplicity by day; no terms (Lilly rejects giving him terms in the northern signs); always direct; mean motion 59'08".
quote: He hath onely the Signe of ♌ for his House, and ♒ for his House-Detriment. He is Exalted in the 19 degree of ♈, and receives his Fall in 19 ♎
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XI 'Of the Sun, and his generall and particular significations', p.69 [PDF p.103]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Hot and dry but more temperate than Mars; masculine, diurnal; equivalent to a fortune when well dignified.
quote: He is naturally Hot, Dry, but more temperate then ♂; is a Masculine, Diurnall Planet, Equivalent, if well dignified to a Fortune
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XI 'Of the Sun, and his generall and particular significations', p.70 [PDF p.104]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Well dignified: faithful, keeps promises, desire to rule, prudent, of incomparable judgment, majestic, industrious for honour, grave and few in words, secret, trusty, affable, magnificent.
quote: Very faithfull, keeping their Promises with all punctuality, a kind of itching desire to Rule and Sway where he comes: Prudent, and of incomparable Judgment; of great Majesty and Statelinesse
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XI 'Of the Sun, and his generall and particular significations', p.70 [PDF p.104]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Ill dignified: arrogant, proud, disdainful, boasts of pedigree, purblind in judgment, restless, domineering, foolish, a spendthrift living on others' charity.
quote: Then the Solar man is Arrogant and Proud, disdaining all men, cracking of his Pedegree, he is Pur-blind in Sight and Judgment, restlesse, troublesome, domineering
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XI 'Of the Sun, and his generall and particular significations', p.70 [PDF p.104]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Houses Taurus and Libra; exalted 27 Pisces; detriment Aries and Scorpio; fall 27 Virgo; rules the earthy triplicity by day; retrograde about 42 days.
quote: Shee hath ♉ and ♎ for her houses, she is exalted in 27 ♓, she receiveth detriment in ♈ and ♏, and hath her fall in 27 ♍
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XII (Venus; chapter heading on p.72 not image-checked), p.73 [PDF p.107]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: Mean motion 59'08" is on p.72 per OCR (not image-checked).

rule_en: Feminine, temperately cold and moist, nocturnal; the lesser fortune; author of mirth and jollity.
quote: Shee is a Feminine Planet, temperately Cold and Moyst, Nocturnall, the lesser Fortune, author of Mirth and Jolity
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XII (Venus; chapter heading on p.72 not image-checked), p.73 [PDF p.107]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Well placed: quiet, not given to law or quarrels, not vicious, pleasant, neat, loving mirth, musical, given to love-matters, cheerful, trusting, virtuous though often suspected of jealousy.
quote: Shee signifies a quiet man, not given to Law, Quarrel or Wrangling; not Vicious, Pleasant, Neat and Spruce, loving Mirth in his words and actions, cleanly in Apparel
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XII (Venus; chapter heading on p.72 not image-checked), p.73 [PDF p.107]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Ill: riotous, expensive, wholly given to looseness and lewd company, careless of reputation, adulterous, fantastical, no faith or credit, spends in ale-houses, lazy, irreligious.
quote: Then he is Riotous, Expensive, wholly given to Loosnesse and Lewd companies of Women, nothing regarding his Reputation, coveting unlawful Beds, Incestuous, an Adulterer
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XII (Venus; chapter heading on p.72 not image-checked), p.74 [PDF p.108]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Houses Gemini and Virgo; exalted 15 Virgo; detriment Sagittarius and Pisces; fall Pisces; rules the airy triplicity by night; never more than 27 deg from the Sun; mean motion 59'08", up to 1 deg 40' a day; stationary one day, retrograde 24 days.
quote: He hath ♊ and ♍ for his Houses, and is exalted in the 15 of ♍: he receives detriment in ♐ and ♓, his fall is in ♓
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIII 'Of Mercury, and his signification, nature and property', p.76 [PDF p.110]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: The term list on pp.76-77 gives Mercury 'In ♍, 7-13' and 'In ♌, 1-7', which is the reverse of the p.104 table (Leo ☿ 7-13, Virgo ☿ 1-7); seen in an earlier image of the same edition, flag for the dignity-table session.

rule_en: Neither masculine nor feminine of himself: takes the sex of the planet he is joined with; of his own nature cold and dry, melancholy; good with the good, evil with the evil; author of subtlety, tricks, perjury.
quote: of his owne nature he is cold and dry, and therefore Melancholly; with the good he is good, with the evill Planets ill
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIII 'Of Mercury, and his signification, nature and property', p.77 [PDF p.111]

rule_en: Well dignified: subtle and politic brain, excellent disputant or logician, eloquent, searcher of mysteries, learns without a teacher, desirous of travel, given to divination; no one exceeds him as a merchant.
quote: Being well dignified, he represents a man of a subtill and politick braine, intellect, and cogitation; an excellent disputant or Logician, arguing with learning and discretion
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIII 'Of Mercury, and his signification, nature and property', p.77 [PDF p.111]

rule_en: Ill placed/dignified: troublesome wit, frantic, tongue and pen against everyone, wastes estate in prating, great liar, boaster, busybody, tale-carrier, given to wicked arts; easily believes, constant in nothing.
quote: A troublesome wit, a kinde of Herenetick man, his tongue and Pen against every man, wholly bent to foole his estate and time in prating and trying nice conclusions to no purpose
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIII 'Of Mercury, and his signification, nature and property', p.77 [PDF p.111]

rule_en: House Cancer, detriment Capricorn; exalted 3 Taurus; fall 3 Scorpio; rules the earthy triplicity by night; no terms. Mean motion 13 deg 10' 36", never more than 15 deg 02' in 24 hours; never retrograde, but when slower than 13 deg 10' a day she is 'equivalent to a Retrograde Planet'.
quote: She hath the Signe ♋ for her house, and ♑ for her detriment; she is exalted in 3 ♉, and hath her fall in 3 grad. ♏
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIIII 'Of the Moon her properties and significations', p.80 [PDF p.114]

rule_en: Feminine, nocturnal, cold, moist and phlegmatic.
quote: She is a Feminine, Nocturnall Planet, Cold, Moyst and Flegmatique
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIIII 'Of the Moon her properties and significations', p.81 [PDF p.115]

rule_en: Well placed or dignified: composed manners, soft, tender, lover of honest sciences, delighter in novelties, apt to change habitation, unsteadfast, timorous, prodigal, easily frighted, loving peace; a mechanic learns many occupations.
quote: She signifieth one of composed Manners, a soft, tender creature, a Lover of al honest and ingenuous Sciences, a Searcher of, and Delighter in Novelties, naturally propense to flit and shift his Habitation, unstedfast
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIIII 'Of the Moon her properties and significations', p.81 [PDF p.115]

rule_en: Ill: a mere vagabond, idle, hating labour, drunkard, sot, without spirit or forecast, content to live beggarly, content in no condition of life.
quote: A meer Vagabond, idle Person, hating Labour, a Drunkard, a Sot, one of no Spirit or Forecast, delighting to live beggarly and carelesly, one content in no condition of Life
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book I, Chap. XIIII 'Of the Moon her properties and significations', p.81 [PDF p.115]

rule_en: Lilly's order of judging a nativity (Book III contents): things considerable before judgment (524); length of life (525); hyleg/aphaeta and the killing planet (527); Lord of the Geniture (531); complexion/temperament (532); manners (534) and their quality from the planets (539); understanding (543); stature and form (546-549); general fortune or misery (551); then house by house: 2nd riches (553-562), 3rd brethren (564-568), 4th parents (569-575), 6th infirmities and servants (576-586), 7th marriage (586-602), 5th children (603-605), 9th journeys and religion (606-613), 10th honour (615-623) and profession (624-633), 11th friends (634), 12th enemies, imprisonment, violent death (639-646); then directions (648 ff.), profections (715), revolutions (734), transits.
quote: Of the Lord of the Geniture, 531 Of the Complexion, temperament of the body, quality of Planets and Signes, 532 Manners of the Native, 534
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), The Contents (third Book), unpaginated front matter sig. (c 3) [PDF pp.55-56]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: Order and page numbers read from the contents pages (PDF pp.55-56); entries from p.634 onward and the directions/profections/revolutions entries were read from the contents OCR of another copy of the same edition and checked against the chapter pages cited below, not from these contents images. Note the 5th house is treated after the 7th; no separate 8th-house section was seen in the contents (death is treated under length of life/hyleg and violent death under the 12th).

rule_en: Before judging: rectify the nativity by accidents; take the fortitudes and debilities of all planets and the Part of Fortune; note houses, antiscia and contra-antiscia, and nearby fixed stars of 1st/2nd magnitude with small latitude.
quote: In the first place having rectified your Nativity by Accidents, which alone of all other wayes is most certaine; in the next place you must carefully take the fortitudes and debilities of all the Planets and ⊗
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CII 'Of things considerable before judgement be given upon a Nativity', p.524 [PDF p.558]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Lord of the Geniture = the planet with most essential AND accidental dignities in the figure, best posited and most elevated; a near-equal planet participates. Lilly rejects Firmicus's rule; notes others use most essential dignities in Asc, MC, Sun, Moon and Part of Fortune.
quote: I am cleerly of this opinion, viz. That Planet who hath most essentiall and accidentall dignities in the Figure, and is posited best, and elevated most in the Scheame, that he ought to be Lord of the Geniture
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CV 'Of the Lord of the Geniture', p.531 [PDF p.565]; sentence ends p.532
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Temperament: collect testimonies of hot, moist, cold, dry from significators and signs; hot+moist sanguine, cold+moist phlegmatic, hot+dry choleric, cold+dry melancholic. Opposite qualities cancel; the Lord of Geniture and Horoscope counts threefold; the Moon in the ascendant counts twice.
quote: If Heat and Moysture overcome, the Native is of Sanguine Complexion: if Cold and Moysture, then he is Phlegmatick: if Heat and Drinesse, then cholerick: if Cold and Drinesse, then Melancholly
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, complexion/temperament chapter (begins p.532 per contents; heading not image-checked), p.534 [PDF p.568]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: Rule and its weighting (Lord of Geniture threefold, Moon in Asc twice) image-checked on p.534; Chap. CVII on manners starts lower on the same page.

rule_en: Quality of the mind (manners): a planet in the ascending (or intercepted) sign is principal significator of manners, with any planet having dignity in its place; judge the significator and his dispositor (benefic and strong = laudable manners; malefic or afflicted and weak = corrupt). Mercury takes the nature of the planet he conjoins or in whose dignity he is; ☊ equals ♃, ☋ equals ♄ and ♂. Luminaries in the Horoscope matter little unless very strong.
quote: First, if any Planet do occupy the Sign ascending, or which is intercepted, he shall be principall Significator of Manners
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CVII 'Of the Manners of the Native or Child', p.535 [PDF p.569]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Second rule of manners: weigh the significator together with his dispositor.
quote: Secondly, consider that Planet who is the Significator, and his Dispositor; for if he be a benevolent Planet, or in aspect with such, and strong, he denotes laudable or compleat Manners, according to his nature
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CVII, p.535 [PDF p.569]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Worst manners come from the infortunes joined together, or with Mercury in the 7th, 8th or 9th houses.
quote: the worst manners are from the Infortunes, when joyned to one another, or with ☿ in the 7th, 8th or 9th houses
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, closing rule of the manners section, just before Chap. CIX, p.543 [PDF p.577]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Wit/understanding: from Mercury and his configuration with the Moon; both well placed and in good aspect = excellent wit; square, opposition or no aspect = dull capacity. Mercury stronger than the Moon (in commanding signs) = reason masters passions.
quote: Significations of the Wit and Intellect are taken especially from ☿ and his configuration with the ☽, for he governes the rationall Soule and animall Spirits in the Braine
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CIX 'Of the Wit or Understanding of the Native', p.543 [PDF p.577]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Significators of wealth: (1) the cusp of the 2nd (from 5 deg before it to 5 deg before the 3rd) and its lord; (2) lord of any sign intercepted in the 2nd; (3) the Part of Fortune and its lord, and Jupiter, general significator of wealth; (4) planets in the 2nd (nearer the cusp = more evident). Ptolemy's method: the dispositors of the Part of Fortune and their aspects.
quote: Thirdly, ⊗ and his Lord, and ♃, a generall Significator of Wealth
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, 'The second House of Riches, or the Goods of Fortune', p.552 [PDF p.586]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: Chap. CXIIII 'Whether the Native shall be Rich' follows on p.553.

rule_en: Men's marriage: Venus and the Moon principally, then the 7th house and its lord, then planets in the 7th. Both Venus and Moon in barren signs (Gemini, Leo, Virgo) and cadent houses (6, 9, 12, and the 8th for its malignancy) argue a single life or aversion from marriage.
quote: First, you must understand that in the Marriages of Men ♀ and the ☽ are principally to be observed. Secondly, the seventh House and Lord thereof.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, 'The seventh House... Of Marriage: and first of Mens Marriages', p.587 [PDF p.621]; running head misprinted '787'
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: Women's marriage begins p.600 per contents (significators not extracted).

rule_en: Profession (magistery): significators Mars, Venus, Mercury (Mercury = wisdom and parts of mind, Mars = strength to endure, Venus = delight). Whichever is in the 10th, 1st or 7th in its own dignities, not combust or under beams, signifies the art; else one of the three that rules the MC sign and is in essential dignity (not peregrine or in fall); else the one partilly aspecting the Moon (strongest, best and most partile aspect, sinister before dexter); else the one aspecting the Moon within her orbs, unafflicted; else the one rising before the Sun. Failing the first two rules the native follows some ignoble trade.
quote: You are to consider ♂ ♀ and ☿; ☿ shewes the Wisdome and parts of the mind; ♂ the Strength of body to endure; ♀ the Delight
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLVIII 'Of the Magistery, Exercitation or Profession of the Native', p.625 [PDF p.659]; chapter begins p.624
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Three questions in judging profession: whether the native shall have any profession at all; what kind; and what fortune and fame he shall have in it.
quote: Three things are wont to be considered in this Judgement.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CXLVIII, p.624 [PDF p.658]; items continue p.625
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Honour/dignity (10th house) is judged from the two luminaries, the Sun, the Moon, the Mid-heaven, the ascendant and fixed stars (per contents pp.615-623).
quote: Rules from the two Laminaries, 617
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), The Contents (third Book), unpaginated front matter sig. (c 3) [PDF p.56]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: Only the contents were checked for this topic; the chapter text pp.615-623 was not extracted. 'Laminaries' is the printed spelling.

rule_en: Annual profection: one whole sign (30 deg) per solar year, counted from the radical ascendant degree in order of signs (e.g. Asc 6 Gemini: year 1 from 6 Gemini to 6 Cancer; year 2 from 6 Cancer to 6 Leo...); cycle repeats every 12 years. Every house cusp keeps its radical degree and minute, only the sign advances.
quote: Profection is threefold; one Annuall, wherein we give thirty degrees, or one whole Signe to a solar yeer
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVI 'Of annuall Profections, and by what meanes to find out the Profectionall Signe of every yeer', p.715 [PDF p.749]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: The profectional year begins at the solar return (the Sun's return to its radical degree and minute), not on the calendar birthday.
quote: you must begin the yeer of Profection, at what time the ☉ returnes to the degree and minute he was in at the Radix, and for this cause it is called a Solar yeer
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVI, p.716 [PDF p.750]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Monthly profection: one sign per profectional month, the year divided into 13 equal parts; diurnal profection: one sign per 2 days 3 h 54 min. Lilly uses only annual profections, calling the others over-scrupulous.
quote: I will onely proceed to annuall Profections, holding this opinion, That if one should follow the nicenesse of the Ancients in every particular, it were impossible to judge one Nativity exactly in halfe a yeers time.
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVI, p.716 [PDF p.750]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: Judging a profection figure: examine the profected ascending sign's radical house and condition (angle/succedent/cadent, its lord, exaltation and triplicity rulers, planets, Part of Fortune or antiscia there, aspects, fixed stars, light/dark degrees). If the profected sign is free from affliction and its lord is direct, strong and well placed both in the radix and in the annual solar-return figure, the year will be successful.
quote: In the first place consider the Sign ascending in the Profection, what place it had in the Radix
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVIII 'How to judge upon a Figure of Profections', p.726 [PDF p.760]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)

rule_en: For yearly health consider five things: the sign of the profection; the terms the Horoscope (directed) comes to; the terms the Aphaeta (hyleg) is in; the position of the Moon; the ascendant of the annual revolution of the Sun.
quote: The Signe of the Profection. 2. The termes unto which the Horoscope comes. 3. The termes in which the Aptæta is at that time. 4. The position of the ☽. 5. The Ascendant
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVIII, p.726 [PDF p.760]
url_or_file: ~/Downloads/horary_sources/lilly1647/b30338724.pdf (Wellcome copy, archive.org item b30338724); page image re-rendered to .research/sources/lilly/img/leafNNN.png (NNN = PDF page - 1)
notes: 'Aptæta' as printed (misprint for Aphæta); item 5 continues 'of the Figure in the Annuall resolution of the ☉'.

rule_en: Lord of the year = ruler of the sign ascending in the profection. When the profected ascendant spans two signs within the year, each ruler governs for the part of the year proportional to the degrees (Lilly's worked example converts 23 deg 23' to 284 days). Lord of the year strong in the radix but weak in the revolution = weak endeavours that year; afflicted in radix but strong in the revolution = moderate good.
quote: You must next in order consider the Lord of the yeer, who is ever that Planet that is Lord of the Signe ascending in the Profection
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXVIII, p.727 [PDF p.761]

rule_en: Revolution (solar return): the figure cast for the Sun's exact return to its radical degree and minute; radical Sun must be computed precisely since 1 minute of solar motion gives about 24 minutes of time. Method: Sun's longitude at noon on the return day, interpolate by its daily motion to the exact time (Maginus and Argoli give easier methods). Example: revolution for the native's 31st year by Maginus's method.
quote: a Revolution or annuall Conversion is no other then the returne of the ☉ to that very poynt wherein at the Radix of any Nativity or matter he was
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXXII 'Of Revolutions', p.734 [PDF p.768]

rule_en: Precision of the radical Sun governs the solar-return time: one minute of solar motion error gives 24 minutes of clock error.
quote: for the mistake of one minute in the ☉ his motion, will beget 24. minutes errour in time
locator: Christian Astrology (1647), Book III, Chap. CLXXII, p.734 [PDF p.768]
